subject: PayThrive: sudden request queuing and elevated 5xx — urgent
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena@paythrive.com>
To: sofia.ivanova@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Cc: ops@paythrive.com
Date: 2028-06-21T15:14:00Z
Subject: Sudden surge: ~40k queued requests, rising 5xx and token latency

Sofia / Lauren —

We started seeing an abrupt spike at ~15:00Z: our ingress shows ~40k requests queued against our reserved capacity (PT-4892). Token latency is up (~8x for long-context requests) and 5xx rate has climbed from 0.2% to 3.7% in the last 6 minutes. This is affecting core payment flows.

Quick facts:
- Customer name: PayThrive (prod)
- Reserved capacity: PT-4892 (dedicated pool)
- Impact: checkout auths delayed; retry storms on our side
- Attachments: paythrive-metrics-snapshot.png (attached)

Immediate asks:
1) Can Redwood confirm whether this is a pool-wide saturation vs. tenant isolation issue?
2) Any immediate mitigations you can enable (throttles, burst pools, etc.)?
3) We can join an exec bridge if you need senior ops on call.

We're available on Slack (paythrive-ops) and can share logs; attaching top-level metrics snapshot.

—Elena
Elena Rossi
SRE Lead, PayThrive

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>

Date: 2028-06-21T15:39:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Sudden surge: ~40k queued requests, rising 5xx and token latency

Forwarding PayThrive alert — high priority. TL;DR their reserved pool is showing heavy queuing and elevated 5xx. They report token latency spikes and retry storms from their side.

Jonas / David — can you triage and propose immediate mitigations? Priorities:
- Confirm if this is contention in the dedicated GPU pool (cross-tenant spillover) or a single-tenant traffic pattern (long contexts / token blowup).
- If pool saturation, please assess: short-term weight bump, enable burst nodes (if available), or route to compatible fallback model.
- If tenant-side, recommend per-tenant throttles and KV-cache clear / rewarm for affected model variants.

I attached their snapshot and they can share token logs on request. If we can't normalize error rate <1% within 30m, let's escalate to exec bridge (Lauren — please prepare bridge invite).

Thanks —
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Elena Rossi <elena@paythrive.com>, PayThrive Ops <ops@paythrive.com>
Date: 2028-06-21T16:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Sudden surge: ~40k queued requests, rising 5xx and token latency

Quick status / actions taken (minute-by-minute):
- 15:23Z: Observed QPS spike originating from a subset of PayThrive routes that include long-context churn (customer triggers many multi-turn retries). These requests have >4k token contexts and amplify KV cache pressure.
- 15:28Z: Increased pool weight for tenant PT-4892 by +30% (temp) and throttled low-priority background batch jobs in the same pool. This reduced queue depth by ~45% within 6 minutes.
- 15:35Z: Enabled per-tenant token cap at 2048 for the affected model variant to limit runaway requests.
- 15:40Z: Evicted and re-warmed KV cache for the tenant; pushed a hotfix to reduce KV-lookup fanout in the decoder for long sequences.

Immediate observations:
- Root cause hypothesis: a customer-side retry loop (client logic) produced a concentrated burst of long-context requests causing KV cache churn and per-token compute blowup. Not a wholesale pool firmware/kernel issue.
- Current 5xx is down to ~0.9% and queue depth continues to decline; token latency reduced but still elevated for the longest contexts.

Next recommended steps (runbook):
1) Keep per-tenant cap at 2048 for 1 hour and monitor error rate and latency.
2) If error rate >1% after 30m, escalate to exec bridge and prepare a temporary fallback model (smaller context profile) for PayThrive.
3) Work with PayThrive to update client retry logic and set softer client-side backoff.

Attachments: token-logs-20280620.csv (sanitized sample) attached for post-mortem.

I'll stay with the channel for live updates; can open an incident if needed (JIRA-RI-7843).

—Jonas Weber
Head of Infrastructure, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: token-logs-20280620.csv (CSV, 120KB)]

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>

Subject: Update: Redwood response & 30-min exec bridge offer

Elena / PayThrive team —

Thanks for the alert and for escalating quickly. Quick summary from our side: Jonas and David implemented targeted mitigations (pool weight bump, per-tenant token cap, KV cache rewarm) and we've seen error rate fall from ~3.7% to <1% with queue depth dropping.

We'd like to offer a 30-minute exec bridge in case you want Redwood senior ops + your SREs on the line to agree persistent mitigations and a customer action plan. If you'd prefer to continue in-channel, we'll keep monitoring and share a post-incident write-up within 24 hours.

We will also proactively open a support ticket for a write-up and recommendations for retry/backoff tuning; if SLA credits are needed, we can start that process immediately (subject to standard review).

Please confirm:
